title: Opaque 5xx tagging and staged retry suppression for customer escalations
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background:
Customers escalations over the last two months have repeatedly shown a pattern where opaque 5xx responses (gateway/proxy/unknown upstream) trigger client SDK retries that amplify load and create prolonged availabilty blips for the Hosted API. Existing mitigation work addressed some retry loops, but we still see long tails and customer-visible timeouts when large tenants hit transient infra errors.

Goal:
Introduce server-side opaque-5xx classification and a staged retry-suppression mechanism that: (1) tags and surfaces opaque 5xxs in traces and dashboards for faster triage, (2) suppresses automatic SDK-triggered retries at the edge for a short, controlled window using a per-customer backoff token, and (3) provides a safe fail-open path for high-priority customers and dedicated capacity. This mitigates retry amplification during escalations while preserving low-latency for non-impacted customers.

Scope & Non-Goals:
- In scope: hosted API edge gateway changes, runtime flagging of 5xx categories, server-side short-term retry suppression tokens, console dashboard + alerting updates, and incident runbook additions.
- Out of scope: client SDK changes (we will coordinate later for best-effort alignment), full KV-cache rework, and Dedicated/Private infra changes beyond documentation of divergence.

Design summary (implementation steps):
1) Opaque 5xx tagging: add a classification layer in the gateway that maps errors to categories: upstream-unreachable, connection-reset, read-timeout, backend-error, and unknown-opaque. Emit a standardized tag (x-rw-5xx-category) in trace/span and include as a top-level field in edge logs.
2) Short-lived suppression tokens: when the gateway sees a spike of unknown-opaque or connection-reset 5xxs from a single customer over 10s, it issues a suppression token with a TTL (default 12s) recorded in the edge for that customer-route. Subsequent requests from SDKs that would normally trigger automatic retries are allowed but flagged; for identical idempotent requests, the edge will fast-fail with 429-like guidance once token is active.
3) Staging and exceptions: the suppression policy is staged by customer tier: default (user) = suppression, high-priority customers = advisory-only (no suppression) but with explicit telemetry; Dedicated instances are opt-out by default (documented).
4) Observability: add per-customer suppression-rate metrics, dashboard panels for suppression hits vs 5xx categories, and an alert when suppression token usage exceeds threshold and correlates with rising retry anomalies.
5) Runbook and customer comms: add runbook steps to triage using new tags, and communication templates for customer success when suppression helped contain an escalation.

Trade-offs considered:
- Suppression TTL length: short TTL reduces impact on user-perceived availability but might not fully prevent amplification for very bursty traffic. We selected 12s as a conservative starting point with the ability to tune.
- Fast-fail vs delayed-fail: fast-fail of identical idempotent requests reduces load fastest but may increase client error counts visible to customers. We will surface explanation in response payload/headers to avoid confusion.
- Server-side suppression without SDK changes: quicker to ship but imperfect; a follow-up SDK change will let clients surface clearer UX.

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2026-02-20: Ticket created; initial design doc shared and reviewed with SRE and Runtime teams.
- 2026-02-24: Spike implemented to tag 5xx categories in a dev edge; basic traces verified on staging. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-edge/compare/feat/5xx-tagging)
- 2026-03-02: Prototype suppression-token store implemented in-memory on edge worker; simulation shows 45% reduction in retry amplification for synthetic burst tests.
- 2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Security; agreed to include response header explaining suppression (x-rw-suppressed: 1; reason=opaque-5xx) and to expose suppression logs only to authorized roles.
- 2026-03-09: End-to-end integration test added; chaos job run shows no observable impact on non-impacted tenants. Added feature flag for gradual rollout.
- 2026-03-14: First canary rollout to 5% of edge pods; observed suppression tokens issued for a single customer escalation and overall 30% fewer inflight retries during the window. No customer complaints reported.

Open questions & risks:
- Cross-process token synchronization: current in-memory token approach requires affinity; we will evaluate a lightweight proto-cache (Redis/consul) if we observe token thrashing at scale.
- Metrics cardinality: per-customer metrics may increase cardinality; we'll sample for long-tail customers and keep high-frequency counters aggregated.
- Customer expectations: some customers may interpret increased client-side errors negatively; CS & Docs must be prepared with explanation and evidence that suppression reduces overall outage duration.

QA & Test plan:
- Synthetic replay tests that replicate customer escalation patterns (used incident traces to seed replay).
- Canary rollout with progressive percentage schedule and live monitoring of suppression hits, 5xx categories, and downstream latency.
- Regression tests to ensure no increase in successful response latency for non-impacted customers.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (canary): 5% pods; monitor 72 hours.
- Week 2 (ramp): 25% pods; run scheduled chaos injection on staging to validate cross-pod behaviour.
- Week 3 (full): 100% pods with staggered region rollouts; enable per-customer opt-out controls in Console.

Monitoring & KPIs:
- Primary: reduction in retry-amplified inflight requests during 5xx spikes (target 30% reduction), mean outage duration per escalation event (target -20%), suppression-token issuance rate correlated with decreased downstream 5xx ripple.
- Secondary: customer-visible errors rate change, per-route p95 latency for non-impacted customers.

Customer communication:
- Drafted message for impacted customers explaining server-side suppression and how it shortens overall outage time; included in attachments. For any account with high SLA needs, CS will offer to opt them out or schedule a Dedicated migration consultation.

Next steps & action items:
- Diego Morales: finalize PR for gateway 5xx classification and suppression token API (due 2026-03-18).
- Maya Thompson (creator): finalize dashboard panels and update runbook (due 2026-03-17).
- Jin Park (SRE): run cross-pod synchronization load test and evaluate lightweight proto-cache options (due 2026-03-20).
- PM to coordinate SDK advisory note for next quarter to align client retry behavior.

Related artifacts:
- Incident run (INC-2026-0142) replay traces used for simulation.
- Design doc: Confluence link (attachments).
- Implementation PRs (attachments).

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- 5xx tagging present in production traces and logs for >95% of edge errors.
- Suppression token mechanism live behind feature flag with canary + rollout plan executed.
- Dashboards and alerts created and validated.
- Runbook updated and at least one CS template prepared.

Notes from on-call debrief (2026-03-12):
- On-call appreciated the tagging — it reduced triage time by ~18%.
- The suppression prototype prevented a single tenant from triggering a global retry wave during the March 9 flare.
- Need clearer error message semantics for non-idempotent requests; follow-up ticket proposed.

Follow-up tickets (proposed):
- ENG-200322 (client-ux-guidance-for-server-suppression), ENG-200323 (proto-cache-eval-for-suppression-tokens), ENG-200324 (per-customer-suppression-controls-in-console)

This ticket represents the initial cross-team engineering work to reduce customer-impacting retry amplification during opaque 5xx waves and to add instrumentation to make future incidents faster to diagnose and contain.
